# Ps011 — Hollow body lost its inner void: BREP_WITH_VOIDS exported as MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP

## Description

A producer modelled a 10x10x10 box with a 4x4x4 inner cavity. The export pipeline emitted a plain MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP using only the outer CLOSED_SHELL, dropping the void's CLOSED_SHELL. The kernel sees a fully-solid 1000-unit-cubed box; the producer expected a hollow body. Topology is fully valid; the file is clean.

## Reproducer recipe

Outer 10x10x10 cube as CLOSED_SHELL #500, wrapped as MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP #510 (no inner shell). The BREP_WITH_VOIDS variant (with the missing inner CLOSED_SHELL listed in voids) would have been the correct export.

## Expected kernel behavior

There is no kernel-side detection possible from this file alone — but a kernel can expose the representation type (MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP vs. BREP_WITH_VOIDS) and the outer-shell-volume vs. material-volume invariants so downstream code can detect when a part that "should be" hollow is actually solid. Cross-checking with PRODUCT.description hints (e.g., "hollow tank") could surface the discrepancy.

## Notes

Tier-3 metric: inner-cavity count (always 0 for MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP) vs. expected count from metadata. Provenance tier: requires-sibling-pair — bytes alone cannot demonstrate the void-loss defect; the resulting MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP file is structurally valid in isolation. Demonstrating the defect requires both the producer's intended-hollow input model (or its description hints) and the export it produced; the kernel reading just the output cannot tell the void was lost.
